name.text: Calculating the area of an amusement park that is pentagonal

questiontext.text:
An amusement park is the shape of a regular pentagon. Each side of the park measures \({@side@}\text{ m}\) and the height of one of its central triangles is \({@height@}\text{ m}\). Calculate the total area of the park.

[[jsxgraph width="500px" height="300px"]] var s = {#side#}; var h_label = {#height#}; // Calculate true regular pentagon geometry to avoid visual distortion var angle = Math.PI / 5; // 36 degrees var true_h = (s / 2) / Math.tan(angle); var R = (s / 2) / Math.sin(angle); // Proportional scaling var ratio = 500 / 300; var spanX = R * 2.5; var spanY = (R + true_h) * 1.5; spanX = Math.max(spanX, spanY * ratio); spanY = spanX / ratio; var boundingYOffset = (R - true_h) / 2; // Centers the shape properly var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, { boundingbox: [-spanX/2, spanY/2 + boundingYOffset, spanX/2, -spanY/2 + boundingYOffset], maxboundingbox: [-spanX*1.5, spanY*1.5 + boundingYOffset, spanX*1.5, -spanY*1.5 + boundingYOffset], axis: false, showCopyright: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: true }); // Vertices of the regular pentagon var p0 = board.create('point', [0, R], {visible: false}); var p1 = board.create('point', [-R * Math.sin(2*angle), R * Math.cos(2*angle)], {visible: false}); var p2 = board.create('point', [-s/2, -true_h], {visible: false}); var p3 = board.create('point', [s/2, -true_h], {visible: false}); var p4 = board.create('point', [R * Math.sin(2*angle), R * Math.cos(2*angle)], {visible: false}); var center = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: '', visible: false}); // Draw Pentagon board.create('polygon', [p0, p1, p2, p3, p4], { fillColor: '#e8f5e9', strokeColor: '#2e7d32', strokeWidth: 2 }); // Draw central triangle board.create('segment', [center, p2], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#81c784'}); board.create('segment', [center, p3], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#81c784'}); // Draw height (apothem) var mid = board.create('point', [0, -true_h], {visible: false}); board.create('segment', [center, mid], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#c62828'}); // Right angle marker var rad = s * 0.15; board.create('angle', [p3, mid, center], {type: 'square', radius: rad, strokeColor: '#c62828', name: ''}); // Dynamic Labels positioned via pixel gaps var gapY = spanY * 0.02; var gapX = spanX * 0.02; board.create('text', [0, -true_h - gapY, s + " m"], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 16}); board.create('text', [gapX, -true_h/2, h_label + " m"], {anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle', fontSize: 16, strokeColor: '#c62828'}); [[/jsxgraph]]

\(\text{Total Area} = \) [[input:ans1]] \(\text{m}^2\) [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Step 1: Find the area of one triangle

A regular pentagon can be split into 5 equal triangles from its center. For one of these triangles:

  • \(\text{Base} = \text{side length} = {@side@}\text{ m}\)
  • \(\text{Height} = {@height@}\text{ m}\)

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Area of one triangle} &= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \\ &= \frac{1}{2} \times {@side@} \times {@height@} \\ &= {@triangle_area@} \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned} \]

Step 2: Find the total area of the pentagon

Since the pentagon is made of 5 equal triangles, multiply the area of one triangle by 5:

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Total Area} &= 5 \times \text{area of one triangle} \\ &= 5 \times {@triangle_area@} \\ &= {@total_area@} \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned} \]

truefeedback.text: You multiplied the base and height by 5, but you forgot the \(\frac{1}{2}\) factor for the area of a triangle. The area of one triangle is \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}\).
You successfully found the area of just one of the central triangles. Remember, a regular pentagon is made up of 5 equal triangles. Multiply your answer by 5.
You multiplied the base by the height. This is the formula for a rectangle, not a pentagon. First find the area of one triangle (\(\frac{1}{2} \times b \times h\)), then multiply by 5.
